subject: maths
question: P sells a mobile to Q at 10% loss and Q sells it to R at 25% profit. If R bought a mobile for Rs 45,000, then what was the cost price of the mobile for P?
solution:
**Given:**

SP(Q) = 45,000

P%(Q) = 25%

L%(P) = 10%

**Formula used:**

Profit % = (Profit / Cost Price) x 100

Loss% = (Loss / Cost Price) x 100

Profit = SP - CP

Loss = CP - SP

CP = Cost price

SP = Selling price

**Solution:**

For profit% of Q,

25 = [45000/CP - 1] x 100

0.25 + 1 = 45000/CP

CP = 45000/1.25 = 36000

Now, the CP of Q = SP of P

Hence, for loss% of P

10% = [1 - 36000/CP] x 100

0.1 - 1 = - 36000/CP

CP = 36000/0.9 = 40,000

**Hence, the orignal cost price for P = Rs. 40,000.**
